title: Escape from the Giant Pigeon
summary: A production Scratch project pilot with structured teaching guidance, original media, downloadable projects, and a complete build-and-debug path.

seo.title: Escape from the Giant Pigeon | School of Code
seo.description: Build a complete Scratch chase game while learning coordinates, collision, state, reset logic, testing, and evidence-based debugging.

image.alt: Paper-textured chase stage with a start corner and striped shelter

finished_summary: Guide the Player from the lower-left corner to the striped Safe Zone while a comically oversized pigeon closes in. The arrow keys change x and y, the explicit game state prevents conflicting endings, and R performs the same complete reset as the green flag.
game_controls: Arrow keys — move the Player on the x and y axes
Green flag — stop the old run and start from known state
R key — reset positions, variables, costumes, timer, and messages

system_flow: READY resets every actor and gives the player a fair one-second look at the stage.
PLAYING enables movement, pursuit, the timer, panic, and collision checks.
Pigeon contact wins collision priority and changes the state to CAUGHT.
Safe Zone contact is accepted only when the Player is not touching the pigeon, then changes the state to SAFE.
R or a new green-flag click returns the whole project to READY.
teacher_checkpoints: After reset: ask the student to name every value and visual state restored by Reset Game.
After movement: ask which keys change x and which change y, then test all four edges.
After pursuit: confirm the pigeon begins far away and does not move during READY.
After collision: place the Player where both contacts look possible and confirm CAUGHT has priority.
Before demonstration: run green flag, SAFE → R, CAUGHT → R, and three rapid green-flag restarts.
test_checklist: Click the green flag three times; each run starts at the same positions with READY before PLAYING.
Win, press R, and confirm positions, variables, timer, costumes, visibility, and speech reset.
Get caught, press R, and confirm the Player returns to the normal costume.
Hold each arrow key at every stage edge; the Player remains between x -218/218 and y -158/158.
Confirm the pigeon starts at x 155, y 100 while the Player starts at x -190, y -110.
Enter the Safe Zone without pigeon contact; the state becomes SAFE exactly once.
Force an overlap near the Safe Zone; pigeon contact produces CAUGHT, never both endings.
Change each visible variable, restart, and confirm Game State, Panic, Survival Time, and Pigeon Speed reset.
Hide or change a sprite costume in the editor, then restart; every actor becomes visible in its initial costume.

debugging_guide.clue: Check all four boundary comparisons and confirm x rules set x while y rules set y.

debugging_guide.symptom: The pigeon catches the Player immediately
debugging_guide.clue: Inspect both reset positions and make sure pursuit only runs while Game State equals PLAYING.

debugging_guide.symptom: SAFE and CAUGHT seem to happen together
debugging_guide.clue: Keep the not-touching-pigeon guard around the Safe Zone check and set state before broadcasting the ending.

debugging_guide.symptom: R leaves an old message or costume
debugging_guide.clue: Every sprite needs a Reset Actors receiver that restores costume, visibility, and speech as well as position.

debugging_guide.symptom: Panic rises in the wrong direction
debugging_guide.clue: The formula subtracts scaled distance from 100; then two checks clamp the result to 0–100.

builder_challenge: Change Pigeon Speed to 3, test three routes, and adjust one starting coordinate until the game remains fair.
inventor_challenge: Add sandwich crumbs that reduce Panic without changing Game State. Explain how each crumb can trigger only once.
boss_level_challenge: Create a second original backdrop with a new Safe Zone location. Reset the stage number, actor positions, and collision rules without duplicating the whole game.
provisional_note: The sketch-style vectors, layout slots, and palette are production-ready placeholders for this pilot. A human illustrator can refine them later without changing sprite names, costume centres, scripts, downloads, or the reusable curriculum model.

code_sections.title: Reset the game
code_sections.does: Creates one reliable starting state for every run.
code_sections.logic: The flag asks for Reset Game. That receiver sets READY first, restores every variable, resets the timer, waits for every actor to reset, then begins PLAYING after a fair pause.
code_sections.pseudocode:
ON green flag:
    ask the whole project to reset
ON Reset Game:
    set READY and restore every value
    reset every actor
    wait for a fair start
    set PLAYING
code_sections.test: Click the green flag three times from different endings. The same positions and values must return each time.
code_sections.mistake: Setting PLAYING before the sprites have moved back lets collision code read stale positions.
code_sections.teacher_checkpoint: Ask the student why Reset Actors uses broadcast and wait instead of an ordinary broadcast.

code_sections.title: Move the player
code_sections.does: Reads all four arrow keys and changes one coordinate at a time.
code_sections.logic: Movement runs only in PLAYING. Right and left change x; up and down change y. Separate checks allow diagonal movement when two keys are held.
code_sections.pseudocode:
WHILE the game is playing:
    read the arrow keys
    change x for left or right
    change y for up or down
code_sections.test: Hold one key at a time, then hold two together. Each axis should change in the expected direction.
code_sections.mistake: Using change y for left/right or reversing the negative signs.
code_sections.teacher_checkpoint: Have the student predict the new coordinate before pressing each arrow once.

code_sections.title: Keep the player on stage
code_sections.does: Clamps the Player to a readable rectangle inside the Scratch stage.
code_sections.logic: Four comparisons inspect the live x and y positions. If an edge is exceeded, the matching coordinate is set exactly to that edge.
code_sections.pseudocode:
FOREVER during PLAYING:
    if x passes either side, put x on the edge
    if y passes top or bottom, put y on the edge
code_sections.test: Hold every arrow key against every boundary, including two diagonal corners.
code_sections.mistake: Checking an x boundary and accidentally setting y.
code_sections.teacher_checkpoint: Ask why the limits are smaller than the stage coordinates -240/240 and -180/180.

code_sections.title: Start the pigeon
code_sections.does: Restores the dramatic pigeon to a known, distant starting zone.
code_sections.logic: Reset Actors restores position, direction, costume, and visibility. The Stage remains in READY for one second before pursuit can run.
code_sections.pseudocode:
ON Reset Actors:
    stop any old chase appearance
    move far from the Player
    face left, show wings up, and show
code_sections.test: Move and repaint the pigeon during a run, restart, and confirm all its starting properties return.
code_sections.mistake: Resetting only the position while an ending costume or hidden state remains.
code_sections.teacher_checkpoint: Measure the visual distance between the two known starts before PLAYING begins.

code_sections.title: Chase the player
code_sections.does: Uses one transparent pursuit rule: point toward the Player and move by Pigeon Speed.
code_sections.logic: The forever loop re-aims because the Player keeps moving. A short wait controls speed and makes the two wing costumes readable.
code_sections.pseudocode:
WHILE the game is PLAYING:
    point toward the Player's current position
    move by Pigeon Speed
    flap once and pause briefly
code_sections.test: Move in a large rectangle and confirm the pigeon continually corrects its direction.
code_sections.mistake: Pointing toward the Player once before the loop instead of during every chase step.
code_sections.teacher_checkpoint: Ask which single variable can make the chase easier or harder without rewriting it.

code_sections.title: Detect being caught
code_sections.does: Changes the state to CAUGHT exactly once when the Player touches the Giant Pigeon.
code_sections.logic: The outer state check prevents repeated endings. State changes before the broadcast, so every other PLAYING system stops on its next check.
code_sections.pseudocode:
WHILE PLAYING:
    if touching the Giant Pigeon:
        set CAUGHT first
        announce Caught
code_sections.test: Let the pigeon touch the Player from several directions and confirm CAUGHT appears once.
code_sections.mistake: Broadcasting the ending before changing state allows another detector to run as if play continues.
code_sections.teacher_checkpoint: Pause on the contact frame and ask which command prevents a second ending.

code_sections.title: Detect reaching safety
code_sections.does: Awards SAFE only when the Player reaches the shelter without pigeon contact.
code_sections.logic: The not-touching-pigeon guard gives CAUGHT priority in an overlap that looks simultaneous. Only then does the script inspect the Safe Zone.
code_sections.test: Reach the shelter cleanly, then drag the pigeon over it and test the overlap priority.
code_sections.mistake: Testing safety without excluding pigeon contact makes the ending depend on script timing.
code_sections.teacher_checkpoint: Ask the student to explain the nested condition in one sentence.

code_sections.title: Update the panic meter
code_sections.does: Turns distance into a 0–100 Panic value and records survival time.
code_sections.logic: Nearby pigeons create higher Panic. Two boundary checks keep the meter sensible. A separate Stage script rounds the timer to tenths while PLAYING.
code_sections.pseudocode:
WHILE PLAYING:
    Panic = 100 - rounded(distance / 4)
    clamp Panic between 0 and 100
    Survival Time = timer rounded to tenths
code_sections.test: Watch Panic at the far start, during approach, and on contact; restart and verify both values return to zero.
code_sections.mistake: Dividing 100 by distance instead of subtracting scaled distance makes the meter jump unpredictably.
code_sections.teacher_checkpoint: Ask why a game can display an approximate meter even though collision still uses direct touching.

code_sections.title: End the game cleanly
code_sections.does: Shows one clear result using costume, sound, speech, and Safe Zone feedback.
code_sections.logic: Ending receivers do presentation work after the detector has committed the game state. Chase and movement stop because they are gated by PLAYING.
code_sections.pseudocode:
ON Caught:
    show caught costume and sound
    explain how to restart
ON Reached Safety:
    activate the shelter and play its sound
    explain how to restart
code_sections.test: Trigger each ending and verify the other sound, costume, and state never appears.
code_sections.mistake: Using stop all before displaying the result prevents ending feedback and restart scripts.
code_sections.teacher_checkpoint: Ask which scripts stop because of state, even though no stop block is used.

code_sections.title: Restart and test
code_sections.does: Routes the R key through the same complete Reset Game system as the flag.
code_sections.logic: There is one reset definition, so fixes apply to both start paths. R works after a win, after a loss, or during play.
code_sections.pseudocode:
ON R key:
    ask for Reset Game and wait
THEN test green flag, win-restart, caught-restart, edges, overlap, and variables
code_sections.test: Run every item in the page checklist, including three repeated flag clicks and both ending-to-R paths.
code_sections.mistake: Duplicating the reset commands under R eventually makes the two restart paths disagree.
code_sections.teacher_checkpoint: Student demonstrates one repaired bug and identifies the test that now catches it.

scripts.source:
when green flag clicked
broadcast [Reset Game v] and wait

when [r v] key pressed
broadcast [Reset Game v] and wait

when I receive [Reset Game v]
set [Game State v] to [READY]
stop all sounds
set [Panic v] to (0)
set [Survival Time v] to (0)
set [Pigeon Speed v] to (2)
reset timer
broadcast [Reset Actors v] and wait
wait (1) seconds
set [Game State v] to [PLAYING]
play sound [start v] until done

when green flag clicked
forever
    if <(Game State) = [PLAYING]> then
        set [Survival Time v] to ((round ((timer) * (10))) / (10))
    end
end

when I receive [Reset Actors v]
set rotation style [left-right v]
go to x: (-190) y: (-110)
switch costume to [normal v]
show
say []

when green flag clicked
forever
    if <(Game State) = [PLAYING]> then
        if <key [right arrow v] pressed?> then
            change x by (5)
        end
        if <key [left arrow v] pressed?> then
            change x by (-5)
        end
        if <key [up arrow v] pressed?> then
            change y by (5)
        end
        if <key [down arrow v] pressed?> then
            change y by (-5)
        end
    end
end

when green flag clicked
forever
    if <(Game State) = [PLAYING]> then
        if <(x position) > (218)> then
            set x to (218)
        end
        if <(x position) < (-218)> then
            set x to (-218)
        end
        if <(y position) > (158)> then
            set y to (158)
        end
        if <(y position) < (-158)> then
            set y to (-158)
        end
    end
end

when green flag clicked
forever
    if <(Game State) = [PLAYING]> then
        if <touching [Giant Pigeon v]?> then
            set [Game State v] to [CAUGHT]
            broadcast [Caught v]
        end
    end
end

when green flag clicked
forever
    if <(Game State) = [PLAYING]> then
        if <not <touching [Giant Pigeon v]?>> then
            if <touching [Safe Zone v]?> then
                set [Game State v] to [SAFE]
                broadcast [Reached Safety v]
            end
        end
    end
end

when green flag clicked
forever
    if <(Game State) = [PLAYING]> then
        set [Panic v] to ((100) - (round ((distance to [Giant Pigeon v]) / (4))))
        if <(Panic) < (0)> then
            set [Panic v] to (0)
        end
        if <(Panic) > (100)> then
            set [Panic v] to (100)
        end
    end
end

when I receive [Caught v]
switch costume to [caught v]
play sound [caught v] until done
say [CAUGHT! Press R to restart.]

when I receive [Reached Safety v]
say [SAFE! Press R to restart.]

when I receive [Reset Actors v]
set rotation style [all around v]
go to x: (155) y: (100)
point in direction (-90)
switch costume to [wings up v]
show

when green flag clicked
forever
    if <(Game State) = [PLAYING]> then
        point towards [Player v]
        move (Pigeon Speed) steps
        next costume
        wait (0.08) seconds
    end
end

when I receive [Reset Actors v]
go to x: (190) y: (-115)
switch costume to [inactive v]
show

when I receive [Reached Safety v]
switch costume to [active v]
play sound [safe v] until done
